one_sheet.name: Lena Marsh
one_sheet.one_line: Dietitian turned trail food maker who has hiked two long trails on her own meals

short_bio.text: Lena Marsh is the founder of Wrenfield Provisions, which makes lightweight meals for backpackers. A dietitian for nine years, she hiked the Pacific Crest and Continental Divide trails and develops every recipe herself.

long_bio.text: Lena Marsh is the founder of Wrenfield Provisions, an online store for lightweight backpacking meals. She worked for nine years as a dietitian before starting the company in 2023 in her garage in Bend, Oregon. She hiked the Pacific Crest Trail in 2019 and the Continental Divide Trail in 2021, and she developed every Wrenfield Provisions recipe herself with a food scientist. She talks about trail nutrition, resupply planning and building a food brand for one community.

hook_episode.title: Dehydrating your own meals, ft. Nora Quinn

pitches.subject: Guest idea: Trail food at half the weight
pitches.body:
Hi Rob,

I listened to "Dehydrating your own meals, ft. Nora Quinn" from October 16, 2026. The part that stuck: Nora Quinn on home dehydrating, shelf life and the meals that never rehydrate well.

I'm Lena Marsh, founder of Wrenfield Provisions, and I'd like to suggest an episode on eating well on the trail at half the weight. Your listeners would learn three things: how many calories per ounce to aim for, and why most packs miss it; a three-meal day that weighs under 1.5 pounds; and the two foods that cause most stomach trouble at altitude.

Why me: Wrenfield Provisions meals average 125 calories per ounce (independent lab panel, June 15, 2026).

My one-sheet, with bios and sample questions: https://www.wrenfieldprovisions.example/press/lena-marsh-one-sheet/

Would this fit an episode in December?

Lena

Lena
